claim: Project 2025's "Mandate for Leadership" — the 920-page Republican policy blueprint coordinated by the Heritage Foundation and contributors drawn heavily from Russell Vought's Center for Renewing America — proposes three programmatic changes that disproportionately affect rural and small-operator America: (1) the repeal of the Agricultural Risk Coverage and Price Loss Coverage crop-insurance programs (the twin pillars insuring roughly 81% of U.S. food-producing acres) and a ban on farmers receiving both ARC/PLC payments and crop-insurance indemnities in the same year; (2) shrinking the Farm Service Agency and tightening access to FSA direct and guaranteed loans used by small and family farmers; and (3) ending the Essential Air Service program, which subsidizes commercial flights to small rural airports.

sources.label: The Hill — "Project 2025's proposals for farming and food aid: What to know," July 25, 2024.

Investigate Midwest — "Farm programs, USDA would shrink under Project 2025 goals for ag," July 19, 2024.

notes: Each provision is in the public Project 2025 "Mandate for Leadership" volume. The @_paperplanet_ reel's editorial proposition — that these provisions plus the 2026 fuel-price shock combine to drive small operators into bankruptcy at prices favorable to corporate consolidators — is the speaker's synthesis. The provisions themselves are individually verifiable.
